chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهَ وَمُحَمَّدٌ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ هِشَامِ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: مَا فَعَلَ ابْنُ الطَّيَّارِ؟ قُلْتُ: مَاتَ. قَالَ: رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ وَلَقَاهُ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا فَقَدْ كَانَ شَدِيدَ الْخِصَامِ عَنَّا أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ

translations.en: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: What happened to Ibn al-Tayyar? I said: He died. He said: May Allah have mercy on him and grant him radiance and joy, for he was an intensely vocal defender on our behalf – the people of the House.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) inquires about the fate of Ibn al-Tayyar after his death, expressing that despite his strong opposition or debate with the Ahl al-Bayt, he will be granted mercy, radiance, and joy in the afterlife due to his vigorous defense of them.
en.seo_question: Why did the Imam say Ibn al-Tayyar would receive mercy despite his strong arguments against the Ahl al-Bayt?

key_terms.ابْنُ الطَّيَّارِ: Ibn al-Tayyar (a specific companion known for his debates)
key_terms.نَضْرَةً: Radiance or freshness (of face/appearance in paradise)
key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
